title: One-year service contract for helicopter transport in South Greenland approved
notes: Primary operator notice. Contract takes effect 2026-04-16. Two H125 helicopters based in Qaqortoq fly to Narsaq and Nanortalik year-round, and to South Greenland settlements during 1 Jan–31 May and 1 Sep–25 Oct 2026 (months 1–5, 9–10), with up to two and three weekday return flights to Narsaq and Nanortalik respectively.

title: Air Greenland routemap — domestic hub schedule narrative
notes: Domestic hub-and-spoke narrative: Nuuk/Ilulissat hubs; Paamiut/Maniitsoq/Sisimiut/Kangerlussuaq; North Greenland via Ilulissat (Aasiaat, Qaarsut/Uummannaq, Upernavik, Qaanaaq Tuesday chain); East Greenland via Kulusuk up to three weekly to Atlantic airport from 2024-11-28. Structural relationships only — not live departures.

title: Royal Arctic Line — contact, ports 2026, exclusive concession
notes: Government-owned exclusive concession for freight to/from/between Greenland towns and settlements. Lists 13 Greenland terminals (Nuuk hub + Aasiaat, Ilulissat, Maniitsoq, Nanortalik, Narsaq, Paamiut, Qaqortoq, Qasigiannguit, Sisimiut, Tasiilaq, Upernavik, Uummannaq). Structural town-terminal sea edges modelled as Nuuk hub spokes; no settlement red-call feeders.

title: Greenland Healthcare System — patient transfers and evacuations (2025)
notes: Stretcher/ambulance-plane network coordinated via Queen Ingrid's Hospital Nuuk; Air Greenland is flight operator for domestic patient transport. Used only for emergency capability on Nuuk-centered structural air edges — not settlement SAR invent.
